Coastal Forests Recover After Storm Season

Researchers surveying coastal woodlands found that native tree cover rebounded faster than expected after consecutive storm seasons. Field teams measured seedling density across twenty plots and compared the results with satellite canopy indexes collected over five years.

The study notes that mixed-species stands retained soil moisture more effectively than monocultures, reducing erosion along the dune line. Local conservation groups have already adapted planting schedules to favor the resilient combinations identified in the report.

Community volunteers continue weekly monitoring walks, recording bird activity and undergrowth recovery. Officials say the findings will inform shoreline management budgets for the next planning cycle.
